summary: A configuration omission caused the outage: the newly enabled legacy-client adapter configuration lacked the region-header mapping, so legacy-client requests reached the routing function without the required region header and failed. Errors rose from below 0.2% to 38% within two minutes of the 09:00 cutover (E1, E2), 97% of sampled failures carried the missing-header signature (E3), the configuration defect is directly documented and contrasts with the retained mapping in the modern-client adapter (E4), and disabling that configuration restored normal error rates within three minutes (E6). Database health stayed normal (E5), excluding the data tier. The CPU rise (E7) is best read as a downstream effect of elevated error and retry handling rather than a cause, and the 08:54 PDF rendering ticket (E8) is an unrelated coincidence in time. The evidence supports a single sufficient cause; no interaction between mechanisms is required to explain the outcome.

claims.statement: A new legacy-client adapter configuration began handling legacy-client traffic on the invoice service at 09:00.
Invoice creation errors rose from below 0.2% to 38% at 09:02, two minutes after the cutover.
Ninety-seven percent of sampled failed requests lacked the region header required by the routing function.
The legacy-client adapter configuration omitted the region-header mapping while the modern-client adapter retained it.
The omitted mapping in the legacy-client adapter is the mechanism that produced requests missing the region header.
Requests reaching the routing function without the required region header fail invoice creation.
Disabling the new legacy-client adapter configuration at 09:19 returned errors below 0.2% within three minutes.
The configuration change is causally responsible for the outage, supported by onset timing, failure signature, documented defect, and reversal on removal.
The database tier did not contribute: error rate, saturation, and replication lag remained within the prior week's normal range.
The application CPU rise from 51% to 65% is a downstream effect of elevated error handling, not a cause of the failures.
The 08:54 PDF rendering ticket is unrelated to invoice creation failures and shares only temporal proximity.
Approximately 3% of sampled failures did not exhibit the missing-header signature and are unexplained by the primary mechanism.

relationships.note: Two-minute interval between cutover and error onset.
The missing header is the intermediate state linking the configuration defect to request failure.
Removal of the suspected cause reversed the outcome.
Excluding the data tier narrows the explanation to the application path.
The residual 3% of failures has no evidenced mechanism in the package.
No evidenced pathway connects the PDF defect to invoice creation.

uncertainties.statement: The mechanism behind the roughly 3% of sampled failures that did not lack the region header is unknown.
uncertainties.discriminatingObservation: Classify error codes and stack traces for the non-missing-header failures and compare their rate against the pre-cutover baseline to determine whether they are background noise or a second mechanism.

uncertainties.statement: Whether anything other than the adapter configuration changed at or near 09:00 is not established by the package.
uncertainties.discriminatingObservation: Retrieve the full deployment and configuration change log for the invoice service covering 08:00 to 09:30.

uncertainties.statement: Whether the CPU rise was purely a consequence of error handling or reflects an independent resource pressure is not directly evidenced.
uncertainties.discriminatingObservation: Correlate the per-minute CPU curve against the per-minute error curve, including the 09:19 to 09:22 recovery window, to test whether CPU tracked errors.

uncertainties.statement: The reason the region-header mapping was omitted from only the legacy-client adapter is unknown.
uncertainties.discriminatingObservation: Compare the change history and review record of the two adapter configurations to see whether the mapping was removed, never added, or lost in a template divergence.

uncertainties.statement: Why the defect was not caught before production is not addressed by the evidence.
uncertainties.discriminatingObservation: Determine whether any pre-production test exercised the legacy-client adapter path against the routing function's header requirement.

uncertainties.statement: The scope of business impact during the 19-minute window, including whether failed invoices were retried or lost, is unestablished.
uncertainties.discriminatingObservation: Reconcile invoice creation attempts against persisted invoices for the 09:00 to 09:22 window.

actions.statement: Keep the new legacy-client adapter configuration disabled until the region-header mapping is added, since the disabled state is the evidenced safe condition.
actions.rationale: E6 shows the disabled configuration restores normal error rates, making this the only action with direct evidence of effectiveness.

actions.statement: Add the region-header mapping to the legacy-client adapter configuration so it matches the modern-client adapter that did not fail.
actions.rationale: E4 identifies the exact defect and provides a working reference in the modern-client adapter, addressing the root cause rather than the symptom.

actions.statement: Verify the corrected configuration against the routing function's header requirement before re-enabling, confirming requests carry the region header.
actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence of the failure state in E3 by testing the specific condition that failed, rather than relying on the fix being correct.

actions.statement: Stage the re-enablement on a limited share of legacy-client traffic with an error-rate abort threshold.
actions.rationale: E2 shows the failure mode reaches 38% within two minutes, so a partial exposure bounds impact if a residual defect remains.

actions.statement: Investigate the residual non-missing-header failures before declaring the incident fully explained.
actions.rationale: U1 is the only live gap in the primary explanation; resolving it confirms whether one mechanism accounts for the whole outage.

actions.statement: Do not pursue database remediation or treat the PDF rendering ticket as incident-related.
actions.rationale: E5 shows normal database metrics and E8 has no evidenced pathway to invoice creation, so effort spent there would not change the outcome.

counterfactuals.statement: If disabling the legacy-client adapter configuration at 09:19 had not reduced the error rate, the configuration change would not be a sufficient explanation and an independent concurrent cause would have to be sought.

If the modern-client adapter had also shown elevated invoice creation errors, the defect could not be localized to the legacy-client configuration and a shared routing or platform fault would be indicated.
If failed requests had largely carried the region header, the missing-mapping mechanism would be disconfirmed despite the timing coincidence with the cutover.
If database saturation or replication lag had left the normal range during the window, a resource-contention explanation would compete with the configuration explanation.
If CPU had risen sharply before 09:02 rather than alongside the errors, the CPU increase would be a candidate cause rather than a downstream effect.
If a second unrelated change had also shipped at 09:00, the 09:19 reversal would no longer uniquely attribute the outage to the adapter configuration.
